gen-gf-phudu-gf-nanum-gothic: Marker-bold and unmistakable, Phudu holds one line weight right through every curve. Nanum Gothic does the quieter work, wide channels leading into each counter and keeping the text open.
gen-gf-phudu-gf-noto-sans-canadian-abori: Noto Sans Canadian Aboriginal reads open, with every curve ending generously. Phudu is the bolder voice, a display face whose lines never taper, as if drawn with a ballpoint.
gen-gf-phudu-gf-noto-sans-cypro-minoan: Phudu keeps a constant stroke from top to baseline, bold and distinctive. Noto Sans Cypro Minoan lets its cut-back terminals leave big gaps, giving that heavy display line a softer-spoken partner.
gen-gf-phudu-gf-noto-sans-hanifi-rohingy: Noto Sans Hanifi Rohingya reads friendly and modern, its c gaping wide at any size. Phudu tops it with a marker-nib line that ignores direction, so the two feel bold above and approachable below.
gen-gf-phudu-gf-noto-sans-inscriptional-: Tiny counters stay unclogged and friendly in the body text. Noto Sans Inscriptional Pahlavi supplies that, while Phudu brings tails and terminals every bit as stout as the main stems.
gen-gf-phudu-gf-noto-sans-kawi: Phudu's strokes keep a constant width, like bent pipe, with generous openings at the end of every curve. Noto Sans Kawi adds a tidy foil with its open-jawed c.
gen-gf-phudu-gf-noto-sans-nko-unjoined: Approachable is the first word for Noto Sans NKo Unjoined, whose small letters have wide openings. Phudu adds bold, pinch-free curves on top, giving the sans-serif body a distinctive partner.
gen-gf-phudu-gf-noto-sans-old-south-arab: Friendly, Noto Sans Old South Arabian stops its curves before they turn inward. Phudu, a display face that looks traced with one marker tip, takes the loud role beside that plain sans.
gen-gf-phudu-gf-ojuju: The body text reads approachable, with wide s curves barely curled in. Ojuju carries a lightly flexed contrast there, while Phudu earns its keep big and short, lines holding width through every turn.
gen-gf-phudu-gf-pontano-sans: Professional at heart, Pontano Sans keeps its c terminals wide open. Phudu is best at loud display lettering, with every stroke cut to one width, while the body quietly gets on with reading.
